Runner-up: D (Be, Mg, Ca), which fits the mass rule (mean 24.5 against 24) but may not be among the triads Dobereiner himself listed.

Gauss's law for magnetism states that the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero, which means isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) do not exist.

A refrigerator moves heat from a cold space to warmer surroundings, which the Clausius statement of the second law says cannot happen spontaneously and needs external work. Runner-up: A (first law), which only gives the energy balance (heat rejected = heat removed + work).

A prism splits white light into its colours because each wavelength refracts by a different amount; this splitting is called dispersion. Refraction is the underlying process, but the formation of the spectrum is dispersion.

A periscope uses reflection by plane mirrors; a lightning conductor safely discharges static electricity; a thermos flask minimises conduction and convection (and radiation); and a lever works on the moment of a force.

Tensile stress over longitudinal strain is Young's modulus, not bulk modulus, so 1 is wrong. Hydraulic stress over volume strain is bulk modulus, not Young's modulus, so 2 is wrong. Shear stress over shear strain is the modulus of rigidity, so 3 is correct.
Fortran was released by IBM in 1957. Prolog dates from 1972, C++ from 1983-85 and Java from 1995.

Natural language processing, letting computers understand and generate human language, is a branch of artificial intelligence. A database management system and an operating system are conventional software, and a register is a CPU storage element.

A bus is a set of parallel wires that carries data, addresses and control signals between the CPU, memory and other internal components. Hubs and routers are networking devices and a port is a connection point.
Cache memory is a small, very fast memory placed between the CPU and main memory. It is more expensive per byte than main memory, so statement 2 is wrong.
In the binary system 1 GB = 2^10 MB = 1024 MB (equivalently 1,048,576 KB).

The Ramsar Convention (1971, Ramsar, Iran) is the intergovernmental treaty for the conservation and wise use of wetlands.
